ORDER This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the accused in Crime No.469 of 2025 of Payyavoor Police Sttaion, Kannur, registered for the offence punishable under section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC').
3.

According to the prosecution, the accused had, during the period 24.11.2022 to 14.09.2023,
collected an amount of Rs.12,40,000/- from the de facto complainant, promising to provide 10%
interest and also return the amount on its maturity and thereafter, failed to provide any interest or returned the amount and thereby committed the offences alleged.

4. Sri.Naveen Radhakrishnan., the learned counsel for the petitioner, submitted that the entire prosecution allegations are false, and the offences alleged against the petitioner are not made but at all.

It was also submitted that the petitioner has already undergone custody for more than 160 days in relation to similar other offences alleged against him by various other persons before different police 2025:KER:59285 stations and, therefore, the present crime cannot be segregated from the other crimes and the period of custody undergone by him ought to be reckoned for the purpose of releasing the petitioner on anticipatory bail.
5.
Smt. Sreeja V., the learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, contended that the allegations are serious and custodial interrogation of the petitioner is necessary.
6. Petitioner is alleged to have collected large amounts of money promising interest from the de facto complainant and three other persons.
Though the amount collected is Rs 12,40,000/-, the same was not returned despite requests by the de facto complainant and others.

The allegation against the petitioner is serious, however, considering that he has already undergone more than 160 days of custody in similar crimes, I am of the view that further custody is not necessary.

7. In Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi), 2020 (5) SCC 1, it was held that while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail or not, Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case.

sentences.text: 8. In Ashok Kumar v. Union Territory of Chandigarh, [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274], it has been held that a mere assertion on the part of the State while opposing the plea for anticipatory bail that custodial interrogation is required would not be sufficient and that the State would have to show or indicate more than prima facie case as to why custodial interrogation of the accused is required for the purpose of investigation.

entities.text: Ashok Kumar v. Union Territory of Chandigarh, [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. In the instant case, the allegations reflect a failure to return the amount collected as a deposit and the failure to disburse interest due on the said deposits.
Since the details are all covered by documentary evidences, I am of the view that custodial interrogation is not necessary.
However, the petitioner must appear for interrogation.

Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 19.08.2025 and shall subject himself to interrogation.

(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioner, then, he shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.
(d) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall he tamper with the evidence.
2025:KER:59285 (e) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.
